method: Fee text is taken from each broker's own page on the as-of date. Schedules change. This file is not a symbol-search check. Whether a fund ticker showed up in a logged-in symbol search is stored on each fund in funds.json. Referral URLs, when they exist, live in site.config.json and stay empty until a real program link is added.

items.us_stocks: The trade fee schedule describes buying and selling US-listed securities from a CAD account and from a USD account.
items.fx: From a CAD account, the currency conversion fee on a US-listed trade is 1.5%, applied to Wealthsimple's corporate exchange rate, which is a live rate that includes a spread. With a USD account, trading US-listed securities from US dollars already in the account has no currency conversion fee. Converting cash between CAD and USD is 1.5% under $10,000, 1.0% from $10,000 to $24,999.99, 0.5% from $25,000 to $99,999.99, and 0% at $100,000 and over, still applied to that corporate rate.
items.usd_account: A USD-account upgrade is $10 CAD a month plus tax after a 30-day trial, or included at Premium or Generation. Wealthsimple lists TFSA, RRSP, FHSA and non-registered accounts as eligible.

items.us_stocks: Online trades of stocks and ETFs listed in Canada or the United States are $0 commission. Currency conversion, and a US SEC fee on sales, can still apply.
items.fx: The currency exchange fee is 1.5%, included in the foreign exchange rate. Accounts are dual-currency, so a US-dollar balance can cover a US trade without a forced conversion, including in a registered account if you have not chosen to settle every trade in CAD.
items.usd_account: Dual-currency accounts are part of the account. There is no separate monthly USD-account fee on the pricing page we read.
items.ipo: Questrade's IPO centre says that, as a Canadian brokerage, it generally lists Canadian IPOs, or US deals that are looking for buyers outside the United States. It says that in most cases a US IPO is filled at home and Canadian residents cannot take part. When a deal is offered, the minimum commitment is $5,000, and an oversubscribed deal can be cut back. One current pricing page lists IPO and new-issue buys as free, with a $5,000 minimum. A transaction-fee table on another Questrade page still shows $24.95 to buy IPOs and new issues. Those two pages do not match. Check the schedule inside your account.

items.us_stocks: RBC Direct Investing trades Canada and US stocks. Its pricing page, marked effective August 1, 2025, lists $9.95 per online or mobile stock trade for established accounts under 150 trades a quarter, and $6.95 at 150 trades or more. New-investor GoSmart accounts include 50 commission-free stock and ETF trades a year. Read the full table on the pricing page before you rely on a row.
items.fx: RBC publishes a foreign-exchange spread and says it can change without notice. Up to $24,999 USD the listed spread is 1.6%. It is 1.0% from $25,000 to $99,999, 0.6% from $100,000 to $499,999, 0.4% from $500,000 to $999,999, 0.2% from $1,000,000 to $1,999,999, and no more than 0.1% at $2,000,000 and above. If the security's currency is not the account currency, RBC says the lowest spread is capped at the $100,000 to $499,999 tier. Settling in US dollars has no extra RBC fee.
items.fx_short: RBC spread from 1.6% on smaller amounts
items.usd_account: You can hold US dollars in the account. RBC says settling in US dollars does not add a fee on top of the usual commission.
items.ipo: RBC's commission schedule says no commission is charged to buy new stock issues, when those issues are available. Availability is the part this site has not confirmed for any coming US IPO.

items.us_stocks: Qtrade's pricing page lists equities at $0 and says US securities settle in US dollars, with currency conversion possible depending on the account. Its customer disclosure lists Canadian and US stocks among the products clients can trade.
items.fx: Qtrade does not publish a fixed conversion percent. It says it may earn revenue on the foreign-exchange spread. A US-dollar registered RSP, RIF or TFSA (not an FHSA) is listed at US$15 per quarter per account.
items.ipo: The customer disclosure lists new issues, including initial public offerings, secondary offerings and treasury offerings. It does not say a US IPO allocation will be offered to Canadian clients.
